# Loadly — Freight and Trucking Guides

> Loadly (loadlyapp.com) is an independent publication that explains how trucking and freight rules work, starting in the United States. Each guide is built from primary sources such as the Code of Federal Regulations, statutes and published industry standards, works the arithmetic through where numbers are involved, and lists its sources at the end. The website is a set of guides and free calculators. It has no marketplace or freight-listing pages.

## Site Index & Entry Points

- **Primary URL**: https://loadlyapp.com
- **Guides**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/blog
- **Free calculators**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/tools
- **Sitemap Index**: https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap.xml (static pages: https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap-static.xml; guides: https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap-blogs-1.xml)
- **RSS**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/feed-1.xml
- **Editor**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/author/eren-simsir
- **Editorial Policy**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/editorial-policy
- **Full context**: https://loadlyapp.com/llms-full.txt

## Language

Loadly is published in **English only**. Requests under another language prefix (for example `/tr/...` or `/de/...`) permanently redirect (301) to the English equivalent. The only exception is a Turkish-language data-protection notice at `/tr/privacy-policy`, which is `noindex`.

## What the Guides Cover

- **Drivers and vehicles**: hours of service, CDL classes and endorsements, roadside inspections, driver qualification files, axle and gross weight limits, cargo securement, hazardous materials placarding, box trucks, cargo vans and pickups by weight class
- **Brokers, carriers and shippers**: what a freight broker is, broker bonds and trust funds, how to check a trucking company, shipper, carrier and consignee roles and the bill of lading, load boards, freight claims, factoring, minimum liability insurance, dispatching
- **LTL shipping**: LTL versus parcel and full truckload, freight class and density
- **Pay and terms**: truck driver pay from federal wage data, a glossary of freight terms with the source of each definition
- **Importing**: the Importer Security Filing (ISF 10+2)

Each guide separates what a rule says from industry usage, uses invented numbers only as clearly labelled examples, and says what it leaves out.

## Free Calculators

LTL density, Federal Bridge Formula, rate per mile, dimensional weight, fuel cost and detention fee. Each has a written guide, a worked example and sources, and runs in the browser without sending what you enter.

## Structured Data & Schema

- **All pages**: `WebSite` + `Organization` + `Person` (founder and editor)
- **Blog List**: `FAQPage` (the questions and answers are shown on the page)
- **Guides**: `BlogPosting` (headline, author, publisher, wordCount, dates, image, `citation` for the listed sources) + `BreadcrumbList`, plus `FAQPage` where the guide has a question-and-answer section
- **Calculators**: `WebApplication` + `FAQPage` + `BreadcrumbList`

## Crawling Guidelines

- Public content pages (home, guides, calculators, about, contact, advertise, privacy, terms, cookie policy, editorial policy, accessibility, author page) are indexable with `robots: index, follow`
- The website has no marketplace or listing pages (`/en/marketplace` returns 404) and lists none in its sitemaps
- Account pages (login, register, dashboard, profile, messages) exist for the Android app's sign-in flow; they are `noindex` and blocked in robots.txt
- Pages are rendered on the server, so the full text is in the HTML without running JavaScript
- `Crawl-delay` is set for Yandex, Mail.ru, Baidu, Sogou, 360, CocCoc, Bytespider and Rambler. Every named crawler group in robots.txt repeats the same private-path Disallow list
